concepts.def: A tiny nucleus of protons and neutrons with electrons in shells.
Types of nuclear radiation with different penetration and ionising power.
Time for half the undecayed nuclei to decay.
Splitting a large nucleus, releasing energy.
Joining small nuclei, releasing energy (powers stars).

walkthroughs.body_html:
Particles & Medical Physics — a core area of A-Level Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Particles & Medical Physics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Particles & Medical Physics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A proton consists of which quarks?
options: udd
uud
uds
uuu

mcqs.q: In β⁻ decay, the exchange particle is:
options: Photon
W⁻ boson
Gluon
Z boson

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a fundamental particle: proton, electron, or neutron?
options: Only the proton is fundamental; electrons and neutrons are composite.
The nucleus shrinks to half its original size after one half-life.
Only the electron — protons and neutrons are made of quarks.
All three (proton, electron, neutron) are fundamental particles that cannot be broken down.

mcqs.q: What are typical units for the Hubble constant?
options: Light-years — it's a measure of cosmic distance.
Metres per second — it's the speed at which the universe expands.
Only the proton is fundamental; electrons and neutrons are composite.
km per second per megaparsec (km/s/Mpc) — recession speed per unit distance.

mcqs.q: After one half-life, what happens to an individual radioactive nucleus?
options: Every nucleus is guaranteed to have half-decayed after one half-life.
Only the proton is fundamental; electrons and neutrons are composite.
It has a 50 percent chance of having decayed — radioactive decay is random for any single nucleus.
The nucleus shrinks to half its original size after one half-life.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Conservation laws”?
options: Boson mediating a fundamental force, e.g. photon (EM), W/Z (weak), gluon (strong).
In particle interactions, charge, baryon number, lepton number and energy/momentum are conserved.
A fundamental particle not subject to the strong interaction; includes the electron, muon and neutrinos.
A fundamental particle (up, down, strange, charm, top, bottom) that makes up hadrons.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Beta-minus decay”?
options: A neutron decays to a proton, electron and antineutrino: n → p + e⁻ + ν̄_e.
A fundamental particle not subject to the strong interaction; includes the electron, muon and neutrinos.
A composite particle made of quarks; subdivided into baryons (3 quarks) and mesons (quark-antiquark).
Boson mediating a fundamental force, e.g. photon (EM), W/Z (weak), gluon (strong).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Exchange particle”?
options: A neutron decays to a proton, electron and antineutrino: n → p + e⁻ + ν̄_e.
Boson mediating a fundamental force, e.g. photon (EM), W/Z (weak), gluon (strong).
A composite particle made of quarks; subdivided into baryons (3 quarks) and mesons (quark-antiquark).
A fundamental particle not subject to the strong interaction; includes the electron, muon and neutrinos.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Quark”?
options: A fundamental particle (up, down, strange, charm, top, bottom) that makes up hadrons.
In particle interactions, charge, baryon number, lepton number and energy/momentum are conserved.
A fundamental particle not subject to the strong interaction; includes the electron, muon and neutrinos.
Boson mediating a fundamental force, e.g. photon (EM), W/Z (weak), gluon (strong).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Lepton”?
options: A fundamental particle not subject to the strong interaction; includes the electron, muon and neutrinos.
In particle interactions, charge, baryon number, lepton number and energy/momentum are conserved.
A neutron decays to a proton, electron and antineutrino: n → p + e⁻ + ν̄_e.
A composite particle made of quarks; subdivided into baryons (3 quarks) and mesons (quark-antiquark).
